compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`DDGSException` escapes the local web-search tool and kills the whole plan-review agent run. A plan review that finds no prior art is reported as a provider failure rather than as a review.

Reported by a client project on `nava-rebar==0.13.1`, `pydantic-ai-slim==1.107.5`, `ddgs==9.16.0`, Bedrock `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0`. Measured failure rate there is roughly 60% of `task`-ticket reviews, each costing about 8 minutes before it dies.

## Confirmed against this tree

Every structural claim in the report holds on `origin/main`:

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` has exactly ONE entry declaring `"web": true` — `T1`, whose `applies_at.suppress_types` is `["bug"]`. So only non-`bug` tickets reach the tool, and `bug` tickets never do.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:502` sets `web_requested = bool(req.web) and not self._model_override`, and line 522 calls `web_search_capabilities(web=web_requested)`.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:157` builds `local=duckduckgo_search_tool(max_results=_LOCAL_WEB_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS)` (`_LOCAL_WEB_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS = 5`, line 134).
- `grep -rn 'DDGSException\|ddgs' src/rebar/` returns NOTHING. The exception is caught nowhere in rebar.

(The report cited lines 532 / 552 / 217; the current tree has 502 / 522 / 157. Same call sites, drifted numbering.)

## Root cause

`ddgs` conflates "no results" with "every backend failed". At `ddgs/ddgs.py:213-223` it returns results when it has them and otherwise raises:

```
if results:
    return results[:max_results] if max_results else results
if "timed out" in f"{err}":
    raise TimeoutException(err)
raise DDGSException(err or "No results found.")
```

`err` is the last per-engine exception, swallowed earlier at the same call site. When `err` is `None` both conditions present as the literal string `No results found.`, so the caller cannot tell them apart.

`pydantic_ai.common_tools.duckduckgo` calls `functools.partial(client.text, max_results=...)` with no exception handling, so the raise escapes the tool call, kills the agent run, and is caught only by the generic provider-failure handler — which reports `llm_unavailable: true`, `llm_ran: false`, `retryable: false`.

Two consequences follow, and both are wrong:

1. **A legitimate outcome is treated as an outage.** For T1 (prior art), finding nothing IS the finding — it is evidence that no prior art exists. It should not end the run.
2. **`retryable: false` is backwards.** The `auto` backend rotates across providers with differing per-host availability, so the same query is not stable across attempts. Retrying is exactly what works, and operators are told not to.

The report's backend probe on one query: `auto` OK, `bing` OK, `duckduckgo`/`google`/`brave`/`mojeek` all `DDGSException: No results found.` Across five representative prior-art queries, 2 of 5 succeeded.

`max_results` is not a factor — it reproduces with `None` and with an integer.

## Impact

With `require_plan_review_for_claim` and `require_plan_review_for_close` on, a signed plan review is a hard gate. When T1's search fails no signature is produced, so the ticket can be neither claimed nor closed through the normal path. The operator's only remedies are repeated 8-minute retries, reclassifying the ticket to `bug` so `suppress_types` drops T1, or disabling the gate. The first is wasteful; the other two degrade coverage.

All 11 deterministic checks ran and passed in the observed failure. Only the agent phase was lost.

## Likely related

Several open `llm-degrade NEEDS_INVESTIGATION on plan-review` tickets (`0b56-ad83`, `2b30-5d6f`, `2ced-55f3`, `602b-4a55`, `812d-7eba`, `8d53-4d0f`, `cb9c-61c8`, `ccd8-e843`) are auto-filed degradation reports with this shape. Whoever implements this should check whether they are instances of this defect and close them against it.

Distinct from the closed `129e-2d88` and `ff64-ca12`, which concern the ABSENCE of a web tool. Here provisioning is correct and the tool is present; only the query came back empty.

## Proposed direction (not yet decided)

Listed by the reporter in rough order of value. The implementer should decide which of these this ticket covers and record that decision before claiming.

1. **Treat an empty search as an empty result.** Wrap the local tool so `DDGSException` returns an empty list to the model. This alone resolves the defect.
2. **Retry across backends.** One immediate retry would convert most failures into successes; an ordered backend list would make T1 deterministic.
3. **Contain the blast radius.** Degrade the single criterion whose tool failed to `INDETERMINATE` and let the remaining criteria still produce a verdict, rather than voiding a review in which every other criterion passed.
4. **Correct the `retryable` classification** for this failure mode.
5. **Distinguish the two conditions** if `ddgs` permits it — total backend failure and genuine zero results warrant different handling.

## Note on the existing docstring

`web_search_capabilities` in `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` documents a deliberate choice to fail loudly when the `duckduckgo` optional group is missing, so a web-flagged blocking criterion cannot silently lose its grounding. That reasoning covers a MISSING DEPENDENCY AT CONSTRUCTION. It does not appear to have been intended to cover a routine empty search at call time. Whoever implements this should not read that docstring as blessing the current behaviour, and should update it to say which of the two cases it governs.

## Out of scope

Replacing `ddgs`, adding a paid search provider, and the broader question of whether T1 should require web grounding at all.

file_impact.reason: Builds the local duckduckgo_search_tool leg (line 157). The primary fix wraps that tool so DDGSException returns an empty list instead of escaping. Its web_search_capabilities docstring also needs to say it governs a missing dependency at construction, not an empty query at call time.
Owns the resolution-class vocabulary and the retryable flag; this failure is currently classified NEEDS_INVESTIGATION / retryable=false, which is backwards for a mode that clears on retry.

Sets web_requested (line 502) and calls web_search_capabilities (line 522); the optional blast-radius containment (degrade only the criterion whose tool failed, rather than voiding the whole review) lands here.
Existing coverage for web-tool gating; the regression test proving an empty search yields a completed review rather than llm_unavailable belongs alongside it.

compiled_state.title: Plan review aborts when the T1 prior-art web search returns no results
